{{Short description|Theorem in mathematics about plurisubharmonic functions}}
{{for|Oka's lemma about coherent sheaves|Oka coherence theorem}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Oka's lemma''', proved by [[Kiyoshi Oka]], states that in a [[domain of holomorphy]] in <math>\Complex^n</math>, the function <math>-\log d(z)</math> is [[plurisubharmonic function|plurisubharmonic]], where <math>d</math> is the distance to the boundary. This property shows that the domain is [[pseudoconvexity|pseudoconvex]]. Historically, this lemma was first shown in the Hartogs domain in the case of two variables. Furthermore, Oka's lemma is the inverse of Levi's problem (unramified Riemann domain over <math>\Complex^n</math>). This may be why Oka referred to Levi's problem as "problème inverse de Hartogs", and could explain why Levi's problem is occasionally referred to as '''Hartogs' Inverse Problem'''.
